consensus_summary: Elementary spiritual teachings or foundational doctrine suited for immature believers, typically contrasted with solid food.
book_summary: The word received without effort (teaching already digested by another), which is the proper first food for spiritual infants but is meant to be worked (churned into butter) toward solid food.
consensus_core_identification: Elementary teaching / foundational spiritual nourishment for babes.
book_core_identification: Received teaching that requires no work, meant for babes.
boundary_disagreement: The book narrows the concept of elementary teaching specifically to 'teaching another has already digested, swallowed without work,' and extends the biblical metaphor by defining 'butter' as the next stage (the word worked toward solid food) before meat.
material_contradiction: None. The book agrees with the consensus regarding milk as the foundational teaching for babes, but adds mechanical precision to why it is distinct from solid food and how it relates to butter.
rationale: Both identify milk as the introductory word or teaching for spiritual infants. The book refines this by explaining the biological metaphor (milk is pre-digested by the mother/teacher) and linking it to Proverbs 30 to show that when 'churned' (worked), it becomes butter—a transitional state toward solid food.
strongest_objection: The text does not explicitly define milk as 'teaching another has already digested'; this is an interpretive deduction drawn from the biological reality of nursing, rather than a stated scriptural definition.
